subject: Private deploy: intermittent return-path loss during cutover - coordination
messages:
From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@brookline.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: NetTransit Support <support@nettransit.io>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production cutover - intermittent return-path drops (impacting API traffic)

Hi Avery,

We cut over the new private link to Redwood early this morning (per the plan) and started seeing intermittent 504s from our frontend to the Redwood inference endpoints. Our app stack shows outbound SYN reaching Redwood but responses sometimes never return; when they do, latency is fine. The pattern is intermittent and correlates with bursts.

Attached is a tcpdump (small segment) from our edge during the window 08:54-09:02 PST. We also captured the gateway's kernel logs which show some rp_filter warnings and 'NETFILTER: IN=eth1 OUT=eth0' style logs. We haven't changed SNAT configuration on our side other than the new route maps for the cutover.

Can Redwood help triage? We need this resolved quickly — the cutover is currently paused.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Turner
Infrastructure Lead, Brookline Health
attachments: tcpdump_segment.pcap
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@brookline.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 09:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production cutover - intermittent return-path drops (impacting API traffic)

Sam — thanks for the quick heads-up and the pcap. We're pulling the on-call network triage now.

Immediate requests to help us accelerate:
- Can you paste the edge gateway 'ip route get <one of our endpoint IPs>' and 'show ip rule' output?
- Can you confirm whether you applied an explicit SNAT for the new peering (we expect persistent SNAT pool 10.48.200.0/26) or if the gateway uses per-connection ephemeral SNAT?
- If possible, keep the pcap window open and add kernel dmesg for the same range.

We're suspecting asymmetric return path and/or rp_filter strict mode on your gateway combined with SNAT translation resulting in packets being dropped at the kernel level. Karthik and Vanessa — can you start with a quick check of our egress logs and any recent changes to our firewall that might drop inbound from Brookline's advertised pools? Grace, please review SLO impact and prep an interim routing rollback plan in case we need to revert cutover.

I'll coordinate a short call once we have the extra traces.

—Avery
Avery Johnson
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Private Deployments
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Sam Turner <sam.turner@brookline.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production cutover - intermittent return-path drops (impacting API traffic)

Folks — quick triage notes (I looked at the pcap + our ingress telemetry):

Observations:
- pcap shows SYN from Brookline client -> our endpoint, SYN-ACK is sent back by endpoint but we see 0-2% of responses not making it back to the Brookline IP within the same path.
- Our traceroutes and the pcap reverse-path look divergent: packets to some Brookline IPs take a different transit backbone than replies.
- Kernel logs from Brookline (provided) include rp_filter: suggested source validation failure for certain source IPs when packets arrive on interface eth1.

Hypothesis: Brookline's gateway is running strict rp_filter (net.ipv4.conf.*.rp_filter=1) and when our replies are SNATed from a different egress IP (or come back via alternate path), the kernel drops them because reverse path lookup fails. Combined with an aggressive conntrack timeout on their egress interface, SYN/ACKs occasionally get lost leading to client timeouts. Another contributing factor could be MTU/ICMP blackholing causing PMTUD failures under burst, but I don't see obvious fragmentation in the pcap.

Immediate diagnostic commands I'd like Brookline to run (safe read-only):
- sysctl net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter; sysctl net.ipv4.conf.default.rp_filter
- ip route get <one of our endpoint IPs>
- ip rule show; show run for any policy-based routing
- sudo cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward and netfilter conntrack counters around the period

Quick mitigations we can try while maintaining security posture:
1) If rp_filter is strict, ask Brookline to set rp_filter to 2 (loose) on the edge for troubleshooting on a short maintenance window.
2) Ensure SNAT mapping preserves source IP block (use a dedicated SNAT pool mapped 1:1 whenever possible).
3) Add an explicit policy route on Brookline gateway pointing return traffic for Redwood's subnets to the expected egress (avoids asymmetric return path).

I've prepared a small config diff with the above suggestions — attached (config-diff.txt). I'll jump on the bridge if needed.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: config-diff.txt
From: NetTransit Support <support@nettransit.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Sam Turner <sam.turner@brookline.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 13:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production cutover - intermittent return-path drops (impacting API traffic)

Hi all — NetTransit here. We examined the pcap and the BGP/flow records you shared. A few notes:

- We do see asymmetric egress for ~8% of prefixes during the observed window; intermediate provider-level reroutes were active (there was a short flap).
- Brookline's edge is configured with rp_filter=1 on interfaces by default. That will drop replies if the reverse path lookup doesn't match the incoming interface.
- We've also seen cases where iptables anti-spoof rules drop packets if SNATed IPs don't align with expected source pools.

Suggested next steps we can implement together (safe, reversible):
A) Temporarily set rp_filter to 2 (loose) on the Brookline edge for the affected prefixes and monitor for 30 minutes.
B) Add a policy route binding Redwood's endpoint subnets to the primary egress interface to eliminate asymmetric return path for testing.
C) Keep NetTransit flow sampling active to watch for flaps; if the provider-level reroute settles, revert rp_filter to 1 and confirm stability.

We can orchestrate these changes during a five-minute maintenance window. If you authorize, we will apply A and B and then provide updated flow captures.

Regards,
NetTransit Support
support@nettransit.io
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@brookline.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 17:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production cutover - intermittent return-path drops (impacting API traffic)

Team — good progress. Summary and action items: 

What we confirmed:
- Asymmetric return paths were observed during the cutover window; NetTransit saw provider-level flaps causing ~5-10% of flows to take a different egress.
- Brookline's edge was using strict rp_filter and some anti-spoof iptables checks. Those together explain the dropped SYN/ACKs.

Action plan (approved by Brookline):
1) NetTransit will apply rp_filter=2 (loose) on the Brookline edge for affected prefixes at 17:45 PST for a 30-minute test window. (NET-7891)
2) Brookline will apply the policy route pinned to the primary egress for Redwood subnets immediately after (rollback steps documented in the playbook).
3) Redwood (Karthik/Vanessa) will monitor ingress success-rate, conntrack metrics, and look for leftover MTU/ICMP issues. Karthik: capture a 2-minute pcap after the change and drop in the ticket.
4) If stable for 30 minutes, proceed to finish cutover. If failures persist, revert rp_filter and fail back to previous routing (Grace owns rollback schedule).

Notes: we've logged the troubleshooting artifacts in Jira: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/NET-7891 and uploaded the config diff + playbook: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/Private+Deploy+Network+Playbook.

Thanks everyone for the quick collaboration. I'll follow up after the test window with results and an updated cutover plan.

—Avery
Avery Johnson
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
